notes: No resistor is used: the button relies on the internal pull-up of pin 2 (INPUT_PULLUP).
The button straddles the breadboard centre gap. Its four legs sit in rows 23 and 25, columns E and F. Row 23 is the GND row and row 25 is the pin 2 row.
Black wire: Arduino GND header pin (digital side, next to AREF) to row 23, column A. Yellow wire: Arduino pin 2 to row 25, column A.
The GND header pin is mapped to catalogue port GND.1. The image doesn't say which GND port it is.
Pushbutton port numbering is assumed: 1 is the row-23 pair and 2 is the row-25 pair, with .l on the left half and .r on the right half.
The USB cable for power and the serial monitor isn't drawn in the images, so it isn't included.
Pin 13's built-in LED is on the board and needs no external parts.
